title: FHIR IG tooling: FHIR packages, Maven repository, SUSHI, Jekyll gems and the compiled AST exporter for the AST refresh
location: fhir-ig-tooling-v3-<ast-export-ref>-<pins hash>-<IG hash>, in the calling IG repository's Actions cache
derivedInputs: the toolchain pins (scripts/ig-toolchain.env: Java, Node, SUSHI, Ruby and Jekyll versions), the IG's sushi-config.yaml (its FHIR package dependencies) and ig.ini, and the AST exporter ref
holds: ~/.fhir/packages, ~/.m2/repository, ~/.npm-global (SUSHI), ~/.ig-toolchain (Jekyll gems per Ruby version; the AST exporter's classes and jars per commit, from its published bundle when its sha256 matches scripts/ast-export-bundles.tsv, else built from source)
producer: ig-ast-refresh.yml on the default branch only: a successful rebuild that missed the key saves it (actions/cache/save)
consumers: the same workflow's rebuild: SUSHI and the IG Publisher with the AST exporter

stateInputs.how: not yet derived from a recorded read set; the producer may read state:mount graphs

refresh.how: a missed key on the default branch saves a new entry; the one restore-key keeps the pins hash, so a fallback entry has the same toolchain and only the IG's packages may differ

savePolicy: default branch only, after a successful build that missed the key
verify: the toolchain is part of the key, so an entry built with another Java, Node, SUSHI, Ruby or Jekyll is never restored; SUSHI is also checked by version before use (`sushi --version` against the pin, reinstalled on mismatch). FHIR packages are versioned by name. The AST exporter directory is keyed by its commit and only used once its `ok` marker is written; a downloaded bundle is used only when its sha256 matches the pin
uses: scripts/ig-ast-build.sh:69 SUSHI at the pinned version
notes: fhir-harness#292 closed the gap CI speed 14's inventory found: the key used to leave out Java, Node and SUSHI, and SUSHI was installed unpinned and only when none was on PATH, so a restored entry froze whichever SUSHI first filled it and a bare-prefix restore-key carried it across key changes. The pins now live in scripts/ig-toolchain.env, are hashed into the key, and saves come from the default branch only (trust class c).
